name: E-money Directive
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission report (2018) drawing on two external studies
summary: The Commission's 2018 report judged the Directive largely successful in lowering barriers to entry: interest in e-money licences and cross-border passporting grew after 2011, though e-money remained a niche market. It suggested guidance on product classification and limited networks rather than legislative change.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

indicators.evidence: Interest in e-money licences and cross-border passporting increased since 2011; number of institutions unevenly distributed across Member States.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Report on the implementation and impact of Directive 2009/110/EC, in particular on the application of prudential requirements for electronic money institutions, COM(2018) 41
literature.title: Report on the implementation and impact of Directive 2009/110/EC, in particular on the application of prudential requirements for electronic money institutions
literature.headline: Overall assessment positive: the Directive largely removed barriers to entry; licences and passporting increased; e-money remains a niche market
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the rules made it easier for new firms to issue e-money, although the market stayed small.
